summary: Bridge proxy lockup triggering 5xx wave and runtime GPU preemption during tenant embedding burst
description:
Issue summary: Customers observed a sustained increase in 5xx responses from the hosted API beginning ~2026-03-13T12:10Z. The spike correlated with a large embedding bulk ingest from a dedicated customer (Acme Analytics) targeting us-east-1. API gateway returned 502/503 to many tenants while serving runtimes experienced GPU preemption and driver resets.

Impact: ~12% of requests to embedding endpoints returned 5xx over a 45-minute window, several dedicated customer requests hit SLA thresholds. Real-time dashboards showed runtime GPU utilization spikes followed by preemption events and subsequent kernel restarts.

Environment: prod-us-east-1, Dedicated pool for Acme Analytics, momentary cross-tenant traffic mixing via bridge-proxy layer.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Simulate a high-concurrency embeddings bulk upload to the dedicated tenant (multipart upload of 100k small items) targeting the embedding route.
2) Ensure parallelism across 200 concurrent streams from same tenant.
3) Observe bridge-proxy queue growth and delayed handoff to serving runtime.
4) Watch for GPU driver hot-reset and runtime SIGTERM followed by 502s from API gateway.
logs:
Snippet from apigw: [2026-03-13T12:15:22Z] upstream 502 bridge-proxy timeout handoff_id=0x7f3a; bridge queue length=512.
Runtime log: [2026-03-13T12:16:01Z] GPU preempt requested by OS (NVML) - driver reset event.
Scheduler: [2026-03-13T12:16:02Z] evicted runtime worker pid=83421 due to nvml_reset.
Bridge-proxy: [2026-03-13T12:15:45Z] hold_count spike -> accept backlog observed, tcp_accept backlog=1024.
investigation_notes:
- Initial hypothesis: embedding bulk overwhelmed bridge-proxy accept/handoff path, causing long-held connections and backpressure.
- Observed tight coupling: when bridge queue exceeded threshold, runtime short-lived overload triggered GPU preemption via driver OOM/hard-reset.
- Secondary amplification: autoscaler attempted to spin up more runtimes but hit host-level GPU allocation limits and NVML indicated thermal/driver thrash.
- Cross-tenant impact occurred because bridge-proxy momentarily multiplexed requests while draining; priority isolation didn't fully engage under this pattern.
- No recent infra deploys in the 2 hours prior. Related PR noted for bridge-proxy queuing improvements but not yet rolled out (github.com/redwood-inference/proxy/pull/1029).
mitigation:
1) Immediately applied emergency rate-limiter for large embedding upload routes for the affected tenant (Acme Analytics) to cap concurrent streams.
2) Drained and restarted bridge-proxy replicas with increased accept_queue tuning (net.core.somaxconn and proxy internal backlog).
3) Temporarily increased dedicated pool capacity for Acme tenant to reduce autoscaler churn.
4) Rolled kernel NVML driver soft-restart on hosts reporting preempt events to stabilize GPU drivers.
current_status_summary: Rate-limiting reduced error rate to baseline within ~12 minutes after application. Bridge-proxy restart and backlog tuning prevented immediate recurrence. Engineering is performing a deeper postmortem and will schedule a follow-up runbook update. Customer notified with initial update and workaround steps.
resolution: Workaround applied: tenant-specific ingestion rate cap and bridge backpressure thresholds adjusted. Long-term fix planned: proxy handoff refactor to avoid long-lived accept queue saturation and enforce tenant-level early-shed. Planned follow-ups include: code change (proxy PR 1029), autoscaler caps for dedicated GPU pools, and NVML driver health monitoring alerting. No permanent customer data loss.
follow_up_actions:

- Infra: add NVML thermal/driver-reset alert with 5m burn rate detection.
- Product: tighten tenant ingestion default quotas for embeddings for dedicated tier.
- CS: outreach to Acme Analytics with postmortem and compensation if SLA breach validated.
